A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Deep Video Discovery system and retain matching methods and experiments. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison. v3 ends with references; v4 additionally contains Appendices A-C.

before.justification: v3 reports original DVD benchmark evaluations, model and tool ablations, and agent-behavior analysis in Tables 2-5 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and additionally reports reasoning-model comparisons, workflow-efficiency experiments, repeated evaluations, and qualitative cases.

M1.justification: The database construction, three search tools, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Added prompts and tool schemas document the existing procedure; alternate reasoning backbones and the fixed-workflow variant are experimental configurations.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate LVBench, LongVideoBench, Video MME, and EgoSchema with the same task and input coverage, including transcript-assisted LVBench evaluation. Added cases come from LVBench, and filtering analyses concern the already-used Azure service.

E2.justification: Table 7 adds DVD using VideoAgent [27]'s fixed workflow as a controlled comparator. Although VideoAgent already appears in the benchmark comparisons, this comparison within DVD is new. Comparator membership in Tables 2-3 is unchanged.

E3.justification: v4 adds a maximum-step sweep of 8, 12, and 15 without transcripts, additional reasoning-backbone configurations, and scoring on unfiltered-response subsets. Main benchmark splits and default settings remain unchanged. Image-packing and filtering-fallback procedures are newly disclosed, without evidence that existing experiments changed.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ablations and behavior chart, v4 adds open-source reasoning-model comparisons, adaptive versus fixed workflow tests across step budgets, content-filtering analysis, and five worked success/failure cases. Tables 6-8 and Appendix B.2 substantially expand the supporting analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix B.1 newly reports three transcript-assisted LVBench evaluations, with mean 74.0 and variance 0.125. v3 provides no corresponding repeated-run or uncertainty information. This is a limited repeatability summary; no confidence interval or formal significance test is reported.

E6.justification: Tables 2-5 and Figure 3 retain their results. New findings include accuracies of 68.5, 57.5, and 57.3 for additional reasoning backbones, workflow-budget results, filtering/subset scores, and case outcomes. Table 7 reports 74.2 versus 70.2 for adaptive versus fixed workflows at the 15-step limit. Headline performance is unchanged.

T1.justification: The clip-count, subject-registry update, and database definitions are retained. No mathematical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or substantive derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: Both versions claim autonomous, adaptive search using multi-granular tools and state-of-the-art benchmark performance, including 74.2% on LVBench and 76.0% with transcripts. v4 emphasizes query-specific workflow adaptation without materially changing the central contribution or claim scope.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations linking workflow adaptivity to search efficiency and explains API restrictions and case-specific failures. It also strengthens the overconfidence explanation to an apparent primary cause of GPT-4o's poor performance. The existing computational-overhead limitation remains.

D1.justification: Appendix A supplies previously absent prompts and tool schemas, frame-packing instructions for Azure's image limit, and filtering-fallback behavior. It also reports API cost and token consumption. These substantially improve implementation documentation; the existing repository link remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds the UI-Evol reference [40] and elaborates the contrast with VideoAgent's fixed workflow. The related-work coverage and broader positioning otherwise remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and behavior-analysis passages receive targeted rewrites. v4 inserts an efficiency subsection, renumbers the behavior subsection, adds appendix organization, and updates the conference footer. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds Tables 6-14 for comparisons, filtering results, prompts, and schemas, plus Figures 4-8 showing color-coded case trajectories. Existing tables and Algorithm 1 are reflowed or relocated, while Figures 1-3 are retained. The additions substantially expand the paper's displays.

improvement.justification: The controlled workflow comparison strengthens support for adaptive search, while explicit prompts, schemas, and service-handling details improve reproducibility. Failure and filtering analyses add useful transparency. However, Table 8's aggregate scores and Appendix B.1's transcript-assisted mean of 74.0 are not clearly reconciled with main-table configurations and results, limiting confidence in the added evidence.
